description: Solo participant exploring the history and legacy of NASA's discarded hardware  on Moon and Mars through creative strorytelling
summary:
Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive Moon-and-Mars map featuring NASA mission equipment left behind after exploration. We developed map markers, a mission directory, and short, student-friendly stories using NASA mission records. The project makes mission data easier to explore and shows where equipment landed or, when known, where it finally stopped.

It matters because these machines are more than leftovers: they mark milestones in exploration and help tell the story of how science was done in unfamiliar worlds. Their discoveries and engineering challenges still teach us about the Moon and Mars, even after the missions ended. By making that history engaging and accessible to young learners, the project can spark curiosity about space science and show how today’s exploration builds on yesterday’s missions. ⁠
⁠
details:
This project has an interactive digital map built for the Abandoned But Not Forgotten challenge that charts the resting locations of retired NASA spacecraft on the Moon and Mars. Displayed side by side on a public web page, users can explore interactive Moon and Mars maps in fullscreen and click on individual ghost hardware pins to open story cards. On the Moon, the map highlights the Apollo 11 Lunar Module (Eagle), Surveyor 3, and Apollo 15 and 16 Lunar Roving Vehicles. On Mars, it showcases Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Phoenix with respective story cards.

Benefits and Impact:

After robotic landers, rovers and lunar vehicles end their missions, they remain silently on planetary surfaces and can easily be forgotten. By transforming technical mission records into a brief, easy-to-read visual map, this project helps students and space fans easily see where humanity's robotic pioneers stand today. Its intended impact is to preserve space exploration history, spark curiosity in planetary science and connect past milestones to modern missions.

Tools & Software:

Interactive maps: Genially

Publishing &Documentation: Notion

Video & Audio: 123apps Video editor.

AI disclosure: Notion AI was used to assist in drafting the text, and 123apps for text-to-speech narration.

Creativity & Factors Considered:

Combining side-by-side interactive maps with a structured report gives a clear idea for exploring spacecraft in two engaging ways. Key factors considered included verifying all mission facts against official NASA records, structuring the report clearly so it is easy to read and ensuring the entire page is publicly accessible without requiring a login.
